what: How many Lunenburg children were placed out of district in the 2002 school year?
why: `placement-counts` holds this from the Special Services report in the FY2013-FY2025 annual town reports. The 2002 annual town report prints no Lunenburg Special Services report and no placement count: its Textract text was searched for special services, special education, SIMS and placement; `special services` hits only Monty Tech's own section (p32), `special education` hits Monty Tech (p32, p34), a high-school staff heading (p40) and a state assessment line (p54), `SIMS` hits nothing, and `placement` hits a senior job-placement programme and a library site ranking (p15) besides 19 instances of replacement (sources/data/report-tables/2002/). — closes: DESE's SIMS placement report for Lunenburg for 2001-02, or the district's own Special Services annual report for 2002.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 2002 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 2002 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (PDF pages 63-65) with no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its Textract text was searched for debt limit, outstanding debt, long-term indebtedness and inside the, and returned nothing. The repayment schedule prints `PRINCIPAL (82% EXEMPT)` and `PRINCIPAL (69% EXEMPT)` beside two issues (p64-65) without saying exempt from what. — closes: the Town's FY2002 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.

what: Which items made up the $182,500 FY2003 capital plan voted at the May 2002 annual town meeting?
why: `capital-plans` holds the approved item list from the Capital Planning Committee report (2010 p14; FY2014 onward). The 2002 report states only the total: the committee report (p12) says `we were only able to have a Capital FY Plan of $182,500.00`, and Article 4 (p77) votes `the sum of $182,500 for the FY'03 Capital Plan` and lists its funding transfers, not its items. Searched: capital plan, capital planning, capital request (pages 3, 7, 11, 12, 15, 20, 27, 75, 77, 85). — closes: the Capital Planning Committee's FY2003 plan as presented to the May 2002 annual town meeting, or the Article 4 motion sheet.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did Lunenburg's Sealer test, seal or condemn in 2002, and what did the fees bring in?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees (2010 p24-25). The 2002 Inspector of Weights and Measures reports in prose (p21) and says why there is no table: `receiving no documentation or tangible evidence of previous inspections, I cannot report to you in the standard format by listing statistical data such as devices and commodities inspected`. Searched: weights, sealer, sealing (pages 3, 7, 21, 47, 50, 76, 107); p47 prints `SEALING FEES $568.00` as a receipt, which is the only figure. — closes: the Division of Standards' annual inspection report for Lunenburg for 2002, or the Sealer's own inspection records for that year.

what: What grade-and-step hourly rates did the town's non-union salary schedule carry for 2002 or fiscal 2003?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` hold the Schedule A salary schedule and classification plan (2010 p85-86; FY2011 onward). The 2002 report prints neither: its Textract text was searched for salary schedule, classification plan, schedule a and step, and the hits are an inspection schedule (p21), the debt repayment schedule heading (p64-65), a school `STEP program` (p39) and the word step in prose and names. — closes: the Personnel Bylaw's Schedule A as in force for fiscal 2003, from the Town Clerk or the May 2002 annual town meeting warrant.
